chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū Maryam, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning the owner of a riding animal that he is liable for what it tramples with its foreleg and what it injures with its hind leg; so there is no liability upon him unless a person strikes it.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الدَّابَّةِ: the owner or handler of the riding animal
key_terms.يَضْمَنُ: is legally liable or responsible for compensation

ai.seo_question: When is the owner of an animal liable for damage it causes according to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding liability for damage caused by an animal. It distinguishes between harm directly attributable to the animal under control and cases where outside interference causes the animal to act, clarifying responsibility in judicial matters.
